title: The bare New York apartment and Earl Bostic's credit reference
summary: Cobb and his wife take a nearly empty apartment near the Thomases; Lionel and Gladys Hampton refuse a credit reference but Earl Bostic gets him furniture credit.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And when we got to New York, the apartment that we had at 498 West 159th, Laverne and Joe got it for us. Right around the corner from them. How it happened, their good friend -- her husband had gone in the marines, and they had

been in for awhile, and she didn't know if he was coming back or not, and she's just getting to the point where she didn't like it there and she decided to move back with her mother and give the apartment up.

So she took her furniture, and left me all the kitchen utensils ... a table, dishes, what have you; chairs, and a couch. Took the bedroom suit. And the couch would let out, and that was our sleeping place. Now I want you to listen to this.

And we're going downtown, and the Strand Theatre, and I bring some of the guys up, my close friends in the band that I'd been associated with, and they didn't have a chair to sit on. I'd say, 'Well, if they're my friends, they can sit on the floor, like me.' And they did ... and we had a ball. That's how you know who your friends are -- they accept you as you are. See, I didn't intend to pretend, because I was a Texas boy, and that's the way we lived in Texas. Honestly. So I said I'd invite them and if they were my friends, this was a good time to find out. Sat on the floor and had a ball.

And when they left, me and my wife opened the couch out, and get in the bed together. I didn't have no credit references. Lionel and Gladys wouldn't give me any, and I'm working for him. You know who gave me my credit reference in New York? Mr. Earl Bostic. When I told him that they wouldn't recommend me for credit, he said, 'Meet me at Spears' on Third

Avenue at 10 o'clock." No, he didn't say 10 o'clock; he said we'll see what the half an hour is from Monday, and gone out, you know, for a half an hour. He said, "Now meet you at 10 o'clock." I said, "Okay. Thank you." I was at 10 o'clock, maybe it was a little behind, and I walked in the door, and I said, "I'm a friend of Earl Bostick's." And you know what the man said to me? He said, "Any friend of Earl Bostick's is a friend of mine. Come on in."

And just as he said that, Earl walked in the door. And we went up to the used furniture department, and picked what we -- and during that time, he had to pay a third down and whatever we bought, it was $75 down payment, and the next day they delivered it, and this was how we grew. If it weren't for Earl, I wouldn't have had no credit references in New York.
